text:
maria: quick question for the collector design thread — do we want agent collectors on every host or a gateway-style central collector for customer VPCs?
liam: +1 to discuss. my 2c: agents reduce egress & preserve trace context, but they add ops surface (sidecars / daemons).
aj: gateway simplifies auth & central processing, easier to apply per-tenant retention/export rules. but spikes can overwhelm it.
maria: exactly. also thinking about pipelines per signal (traces/metrics/logs) — should we allow separate pipelines per customer and per signal?
katie: separate pipelines give great isolation: retention, exporters, sampling, flags per-signal. downside is config explosion and memory overhead in gateway mode.
maria: curious about hybrid: agent for initial batching + local sampling, gateway for enrichment/long-term exporters. keeps tail-based sampling possibility in gateway.
liam: hybrid seems pragmatic. agents do head-based sampling & prefix/KV caching for spans. gateway does tail-sampling and heavy exporters (Parquet, long-term storage).
aj: we need to be explicit about span context propagation. if agent patches headers, gateway must honor original trace ids. also need consistent resource attributes merging.
samir: bandwidth math — per-host agent removes superfluous metrics and tail logs before egress. For large customers that matters. For small customers a gateway is cheaper operationally.
maria: what about security? gateway lets us centralize KMS/HSM usage for exporter keys. But for private deployments we can't assume access to customer KMS.
katie: idea: collector config model: pipeline objects = {signals: [traces,metrics,logs], processors: [...], exporters: [...], retention_days: N, sampling: {...}}. we can render these either to agents or gateway instances.
liam: +1 on config model. need to support dynamic rollout: canary a pipeline for 1% tenants, then 10%. Console wants per-route dashboards and rollout UX.
aj: exporters: OTLP/gRPC to our ingest, S3/Parquet for cold storage, prometheus remote-write for metrics. Make batching/timeout tunables per-exporter.
maria: probe: should agents export directly to our ingest endpoint or go to regional gateway? latency vs reliability tradeoff.
samir: regional gateway gives better rate shaping and backpressure handling. agents -> regional gateway -> central exporters. reduces cross-region egress.
katie: retention enforcement: we should do hard TTL on gateway and soft TTL on agents (agent tries to prune but final authority is gateway). makes sense for dedicated/dedicated-private.
liam: sampling: head sampling at agent for noise reduction, tail sampling at gateway for quality. We must surface traces dropped counts to customers.
aj: telemetry costs: record per-tenant tokenized metrics (ingested_spans, exported_bytes). that ties into console quotas. collectors should emit internal metrics about processing rates.
maria: can we include a small config snippet?
maria: ```yaml
pipelines:
  traces_high_fidelity:
    signals: [traces]
    processors: [batch, attributes, probabilistic_sampler]
    exporters: [redwood-ingest, s3_archive]
    retention_days: "90"
  metrics_default:
    signals: [metrics]
    processors: [memory_limiter]
    exporters: [prom_remote_write]
    retention_days: "30"
```
liam: looks good. one concern: agents running memory_limiter per pipeline could be heavy. need resource quota map per-host.
katie: UX: console should let users preview effective pipeline (agent vs gateway) and estimated cost delta (eg, bytes/day, avg latency). that will drive self-serve choices.
samir: operational: gateway needs autoscaling policies by tenant weight + burst queues. Also sticky routing for partial-ordered exporters (Kafka).
aj: implementational notes: use OpenTelemetry Collector components where possible. write custom processors for tenant-routing and retention enforcement. minimize forking of core.
maria: agree. next steps: draft design doc with diagrams (agents <-> regional gateway <-> central processors), sampling flow, config model. volunteers?
liam: I'll sketch the flow + autoscale requirements.
katie: I'll own console mockups for pipeline UX and cost estimate.
aj: I'll prototype tenant-routing processor and retention enforcement test harness.
samir: I'll run some traffic sims to get numbers for bandwidth/CPU for agent vs gateway.
maria: thanks team — let's sync tomorrow 11am. @otel-bot please create a calendar reminder and link to the draft doc when ready.
otel-bot: Reminder created: Collector design sync — tomorrow 11:00. Draft doc link: https://docs.internal/redwood/collector-design-draft (uploaded). :white_check_mark:
maria: perfect, will review the doc and post questions in the thread. :thumbsup:
